items.en: Hardware: the cache of program names no longer grows without bound. A long-running copy collected the name of every program it had ever listed, so memory crept up the longer the app stayed open
Updates install again: this build is signed with the key the app trusts, and the release workflow now refuses to publish a release every installed copy would reject
Control Panel and Apps & features show the publisher as latiefahmad instead of github

Much lighter on memory: tools load when you first open them, the closed notch's equalizer runs itself down while the notch is closed, clipboard cards fetch their thumbnails only when you look at them, and when the notch has been closed for a while every WebView2 window lowers its memory target

Speicher sparen (Windows): Settings → General can run every window in one process, which measured about a third of the RAM; plugins then run inside the app, so the trade-off is yours to make and it applies at the next start
The terminal keeps 1000 lines of scrollback by default, so a day of output no longer holds the whole app

The first public release: a notch at the edge of your Windows screen with music and synced lyrics, notices, timers, to-dos, screenshots and screen recording, a terminal, an app launcher, your GitHub activity, AI usage limits, live hardware stats, a read-only portfolio across brokers and more

The closed notch comes as a notch, a capsule or a line on any screen edge; its readings row shows cover, timer, Discord call, AI quota, title or lyrics, hardware, brightness, equalizer, clock and GitHub
Click or hover any part of the closed notch to open its tool, and any notice opens what it is about
Now Playing: synced and word-by-word lyrics with translation and romanisation, Spectrum and Wave equalizers, an album-art tint and a player picker
Capture: screenshots and screen recording with system audio and microphone, a Recorder for sound alone, a Camera tool to check yourself before a call, and Find on screen over every monitor
A Calendar from ICS links or CalDAV, with a month view, notices before each event and Join buttons for Meet, Zoom, Teams and Webex
Overview, Hardware with cores, GPUs, network, power, battery, temperatures and drives, AI usage with tokens and cost, and a portfolio in one base currency
Your own plugins as sandboxed web widgets, and parts in the closed row with notnotch-notify, including answering a coding agent's permission requests from the notch
Timer with Flip, Nixie, Ring, LCD and Analog looks, focus sounds for focus sessions, to-dos, a water reminder, a code scratchpad and a Shelf for drops
Themes with an editor, a day and night switch, coloured icons, sixteen fonts and fifteen themes to choose from
NotNotch in 11 languages, Arabic handled right to left, following Windows until you pick one in Settings
Windows is where everything lives, with a first preview for Macs; ARM64 builds, a portable build that updates in place, and a SHA256SUMS file to check every release
